bug_semantics: When an ActiveMQArtemis Custom Resource omits admin/cluster credentials, the operator auto-fills AMQ_USER, AMQ_PASSWORD, AMQ_CLUSTER_USER, and AMQ_CLUSTER_PASSWORD from process-global package variables populated once in environments.init() (environments.Defaults / GLOBAL_AMQ_CLUSTER_*). Those values are then copied into each CR's credentials Secret and broker env. Distinct CRs therefore receive the same starting credentials for the lifetime of the operator process (CWE-1391). A local low-privilege observer who can read one generated Secret can reuse the same user/password against other CR-managed brokers. Red Hat Bugzilla 2362827 states the four AMQ_* fields do not regenerate between separate CR instances.
flaw_origin: The smallest first-write is 36aeb84b3c433d60dd53030199c08a2af20b9bea (ENTMQBR-2846, 2019-09-09). Its parent still generated per-CR credentials in SetDefaults via random.GenerateRandomString(8) on empty spec fields. 36aeb84 replaced that with a package-level defaults struct and init() that mint AMQ_USER/AMQ_PASSWORD once, then Process() and generateSecrets() fall back to environments.Defaults when Spec.AdminUser/AdminPassword are empty. cd47ded78f0c2f5d6892a05899d649c09963f4d9 (2020-09-29) later extended the same init() globals to cluster user/password. 2021-2022 operator-sdk layout migration deleted and re-added the files (9c0dae80 / bb1109d5 / 16f2dc95); those are moves/refactors, not a new BIC. Fix d3482fab6d0060794226c9e5a6fa67d209abc35a (#1130) generates per-CR random strings in ProcessCredentials and deletes the globals.

reasoning: CVE-2025-4057 is a published Red Hat CNA record (GHSA withdrawn_at is null; Bugzilla 2362827 and RHSA errata treat it as a real credential-reuse flaw), so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. The attack path is operator-wide reuse of auto-generated broker starting credentials: init() of pkg/resources/environments mints AMQ_USER/AMQ_PASSWORD/AMQ_CLUSTER_USER/AMQ_CLUSTER_PASSWORD once per operator process and ProcessCredentials copies those globals into every CR that does not set Spec.AdminUser/AdminPassword. The smallest public first-write of that mechanism is 36aeb84b3c433d60dd53030199c08a2af20b9bea, which replaced per-CR SetDefaults generation with package-level Defaults.init(). Immediate parent 40b234bb802b901e37e92262b9fec6facf84df84 still generates unique random strings per empty CR spec field and has no Defaults type; parent-tree grep confirms absence. Later cd47ded7 only extends the same globals to cluster credentials. File deletion in 9c0dae80 and re-add in bb1109d5/16f2dc95 are operator-sdk layout moves, not BICs. The git fix named by the advisory, d3482fab6d0060794226c9e5a6fa67d209abc35a, is the direct non-merge patch (#1130) that lands in v2.0.3 and not v2.0.2, matching CVE.org's 0 < 2.0.3 boundary (GHSA's Go pseudo-version <= b262048e is a packaging overshoot on post-fix main). AI is judged only from the BIC commit object: human author/committer Roddie Kieley, no AI/co-author/bot trailers. Therefore the real vulnerability has human authorship: NOT_AI.
